THE SPLIT PLATE / RECIPE

Lean Beef Meatballs (30-piece Base)

The batch component. 30 lean beef meatballs from 2 lb of 93/7, oven-baked 10-13 min at 425°F. 5 meatballs = 285 cal / 34g protein. Feeds Meatball Parm Puff, pizza night, pasta, sandwiches, red-sauce bowls.

YIELD6 servings
TOTAL TIME10 min mix + 10-13 min bake
COOK METHODSee method
EST. / SERVING~285 cal | ~34g protein

Ingredients

Ingredients

  • 2 lb / 907 g 93/7 ground beef
  • 1 large egg
  • 1/4 cup / 25 g plain panko
  • 1/4 cup / 22 g grated Parmesan

Ingredients — continued

  • 1 tsp garlic powder
  • 1 tsp dried Italian seasoning
  • 1/2 tsp onion powder
  • Salt and black pepper, to taste

Allergens: eggs, dairy, wheat, gluten.

You want a lean, batch-cooked protein anchor that plays with red sauce, pizza, pasta, sandwiches, and quick bowls. One 2 lb batch yields 30 meatballs = 6 servings of 5 at 285 cal / 34g protein per serving. Baked, not fried. Freezes cleanly.

Method

  1. 1.PREHEAT OVEN 425°F. Line a sheet pan with parchment or foil.
  2. 2.MIX GENTLY. Combine all ingredients in a large bowl. Mix just until combined — DO NOT overwork the beef. Overworking makes tough meatballs.
  3. 3.PORTION 30. Divide the mixture into 30 meatballs (about 30 g each). A cookie scoop keeps them uniform. Arrange on the sheet pan with space between so they brown, not steam.
  4. 4.BAKE 10-13 MIN. Until the centers reach 160°F on an instant-read thermometer. Timing depends on ball size — pull at 160°F, not by clock.
  5. 5.REST + STORE. Let rest 3-4 min before serving. For meal prep, cool completely before boxing so condensation doesn't turn the outsides mushy.

If something fails

Meatballs are dense and tough: Overmixed the beef. Mix just until combined — you should still see distinct panko pieces when you stop. The mixing step takes 30 seconds, not 2 minutes.

Meatballs fell apart / cracked: Not enough egg or panko. This ratio (1 egg + 1/4 cup panko per 2 lb) is the floor. If you scaled down and cut proportionally, you may need to bump both slightly.

Dry after baking: Over 160°F internal. Pull at 160°F. Also — 93/7 is the leanness floor; leaner (94/6, 96/4) will taste dry. Don't sub 96/4 turkey without adjusting fat elsewhere.

Meatballs steamed instead of browned: Overcrowded pan. Give each ball at least 1 inch of space. Split into two sheet pans if needed.

Not enough flavor: Salt is the lever. Season the raw mix aggressively — the meatball is going into sauce or on a sandwich, both of which will dilute the salt. Taste a small pan-fried tester before rolling all 30.

Storage and reheating

Store: Cool completely, then refrigerate up to 4 days or freeze up to 2 months (single layer to freeze, then bag).

Reheat: From fridge: microwave 45-60 sec per 5 meatballs, or 350°F oven 5-6 min. From frozen: thaw overnight in fridge OR microwave from frozen 90 sec then rest 1 min. Serve in sauce to keep them moist.

Lasts: Fridge: 4 days. Freezer: 2 months. The bake is what makes them freeze-friendly — no raw fold-in required.

~285 cal | ~34g protein.

Per-serving (~285 cal / 34g protein) for 5 of 30 meatballs. Component check: 2 lb 93/7 beef (~1520 cal / 200P per 2 lb raw) + 1 large egg (70 cal / 6P) + 1/4 cup panko (~110 cal / 4P) + 1/4 cup Parm (~110 cal / 10P) ≈ 1810 cal / 220P raw ÷ 6 servings = ~300 cal / 37P per 5. Flavor target

Tender inside, lightly caramelized outside — not dense, not dry. The 93/7 lean is the ceiling on fat; the egg + panko + Parmesan keep the crumb tender. Italian seasoning + garlic + onion powder is the neutral flavor lane that lets whatever sauce you add later carry the identity.

Brands I use

93/7 lean ground beef
2 lb / 907 g (any 93/7 lean — Kirkland Signature at Costco, ButcherBox, store-brand)
The macro architecture. 93/7 is the ceiling on fat that keeps a 5-meatball serving at 285 cal / 34g protein. 80/20 pushes calories over 400 per serving and makes them greasy. 96/4 dries them out.
Panko
Plain panko breadcrumbs (1/4 cup / 25 g)
Panko binds without going dense. Sub regular breadcrumbs 1:1 in a pinch; sub GF panko for a gluten-free version.
Parmesan
Grated Parmesan (1/4 cup / 22 g — any fresh-grated or Kraft green-can)
Adds salt + umami + a subtle browning boost. Not the flavor lead — supporting.
